title: Meta app secret as the second part of a pipe-joined access_token
summary: A synthetic app secret after the pipe of an app-id-and-secret access_token value, in a request line, a curl URL and a query string that continues with another parameter.
rationale: Meta documents passing the app ID and the app secret, joined by a pipe, as the access_token parameter instead of a generated app access token. The first part is the app's assigned ID and the second part is the app secret, so the secret is the span after the pipe and the ID before it is outside it. The same layout with a client token is documented as not secret, so the shape of the pair does not identify the secret; the access_token parameter, the pipe and the app-ID first part are the context. Meta states no format for the app secret, so no bare-value rule is implied. Which family owns this pair (the app secret, or an app access token) is not settled by the sources and the case does not choose; it states only the span.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#244). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the second part of an app-id-and-app-secret access_token value is treated as a credential and the app ID is not part of the span. Meta documents the pair form and names its second part the app secret (carrier existence only); the span, the value admission and the choice not to attribute the pair to a family are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: There is another method to make calls to the Graph API that doesn't require using a generated app access token. You can just pass your app ID and app secret as the access_token parameter when you make a call
sources.locator: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies, App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

sources.supports: **Important**: This request uses your app secret, so it must only be made using server-side code. Never share your app secret with anyone.
sources.locator: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies, App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

sources.supports: Therefore the App Secret or an App Access token should never be included in any code.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
